name: Fort Carson
tagline: Home of the 4th Infantry Division and 10th Special Forces Group, at the foot of the Rocky Mountains in Colorado Springs.
_note: Army post on the Colorado Front Range (Colorado Springs). Facts verified from official sources (home.army.mil/carson, evans.tricare.mil, DeCA/AAFES). BAH MHA CO046 (Colorado Springs) via the bah_rates single source of truth. Housing operated by Balfour Beatty Communities (Fort Carson Family Homes). High altitude (Colorado Springs 6,035 ft). Corrected 2026-11-10 from the website-page research (Base Guides/page-builder/research/carson-facts.md): housing source was a third-party site (fortcarsonhousing.com, 'not an official military website'), now the Army housing page; Security-Widefield is mostly Widefield D3, not D8; Cheyenne Mountain D12 added as a top-rated district and Falcon D49's status corrected; gates from the official page; 3rd Brigade is now Stryker; prices flat to slightly down, not rising. Removed unsourced tenure claims ('many families extend or return', 'three or more years is common') and the REAL ID line. Medium-confidence flags: base coords (approx), representative off-base ZIP 80911 (Security-Widefield, Colorado Springs).

sections.title: Mission & Identity
data: Fort Carson, the 'Mountain Post,' is home to the 4th Infantry Division, with the 1st, 2nd and 3rd Stryker Brigades and the 4th Combat Aviation Brigade, and to the 10th Special Forces Group (Airborne) and the 1st Space Brigade.
It sits at the foot of the Rocky Mountains just south of Colorado Springs, a region thick with military presence that also includes Peterson and Schriever Space Force Bases and the Air Force Academy.

source.label: Fort Carson 4th Infantry Division units and tenants (official)

sections.title: Which School District? The Fort Carson Decision

data.subtitle: Around Colorado Springs the school district changes from one neighborhood to the next, and so can the tax bill. The on-post schools belong to Fountain-Fort Carson D8; Cheyenne Mountain D12 and Academy D20 earned the state's top rating in 2025.
intro: In the state's 2025 district ratings, Cheyenne Mountain D12 (84.3% of points) and Academy D20 earned Accredited with Distinction, Fountain-Fort Carson D8 (57.1%) and Widefield D3 (58%) were Accredited, and Colorado Springs D11 (48.9%) and Harrison D2 (53%) were on Improvement Plans. Colorado has open enrollment, so you can apply to a district outside your zone.

Metro districts, typically found in newer neighborhoods, add their own property tax (one, Lorson Ranch, allows up to 50 mills for debt, subject to adjustment), and 2026 tax bills rose sharply as temporary discounts ended. Home values were flat to slightly down over the year: Zillow's typical home value in Colorado Springs was $439,542 in September 2026, down 1.5%. The altitude (Colorado Springs is 6,035 ft) takes some adjustment.

recommendations.advice: Fountain (mainly Fountain-Fort Carson D8, about 16 minutes to Evans Army Community Hospital with no traffic, typical home $385,215) and Security-Widefield (much of it Widefield D3, so confirm by address; about 22 minutes, $370,913). Gates 4 and 19, nearest those towns on the Army's access map, are weekday gates; Gate 20 by I-25 is open 24 hours.

Cheyenne Mountain D12 and Academy D20 earned Accredited with Distinction in 2025 and keep it in the preliminary 2026 ratings. Falcon D49 is rated Improvement in the preliminary 2026 ratings (pending one school's results), so confirm the district for any address.
West-side and foothills neighborhoods put you closest to the mountains; a February 2026 Gazette report on county values said values were still going up closer to the mountains on the west side.

On-post housing is Fort Carson Family Homes (Balfour Beatty Communities), about 3,200 homes, with 477 new homes planned. Visit the Housing Services Office (719-238-6458) before you sign anything off post.

source.label: Colorado Department of Education 2025 ratings; The Gazette (Feb and Aug 2026); Zillow (Sept 2026)

sections.title: Gates & Access
data: Open 24 hours: Gate 1 (Freedom Gate, Nelson Boulevard), Gate 3 (commercial gate, Chiles Avenue) and Gate 20 (Roosevelt Gate, Magrath Avenue by I-25). Gates 4 (Bellrichard) and 19 (Essayons Road) are open weekdays 5 a.m. to 1 p.m. both ways, then outbound only until 9 p.m., and closed weekends and holidays; Gates 5 and 6 weekdays 5 a.m. to 6 p.m.; Gate 2 is closed.
Visitor Control Center: Building 1203 off Nelson Boulevard, 5 a.m. to 1 p.m. every day. Visitors can apply for a pass online at pass.aie.army.mil. Hours change, so confirm before you go.

sections.title: On-Base Housing
data: On-post family housing is Fort Carson Family Homes, run by Balfour Beatty Communities: about 3,200 homes in villages across the post, with occupancy around the mid-90s percent in 2025. Of 477 new homes planned, 80 were occupied and 152 under construction in September 2026, and 300 older homes are being torn down to make room for 245 new homes for junior enlisted families.

Housing Services Office (off-post help), Building 1225, 1649 Evans Street: 719-238-6458. Army rules require you to visit it before making permanent off-post arrangements, and volunteer realtors are on site (719-526-7578). We found no official wait times, so ask for yours.

source.label: DoD 2026 BAH Rates, MHA CO046 (Colorado Springs)

sections.title: Schools
data: There are no DoD schools here. The five schools on post (Abrams, Mountainside, Patriot and Weikel elementary and Carson Middle) belong to Fountain-Fort Carson School District 8, and high schoolers living on post ride a bus to Fountain-Fort Carson High. Off post the district depends on your address: Widefield D3, Colorado Springs D11, Cheyenne Mountain D12, Harrison D2, Academy D20 and Falcon D49 cover other popular areas.

Colorado has open enrollment, so you can apply to a district outside your zone. School Liaison Office: 6371 Specker Ave, Building 1532, 719-526-6470 or 719-526-2463. Confirm the district and campus for any address.

data.Care: Primary and specialty care, behavioral health, OB/GYN, pediatrics, and a 24/7 emergency department

intro: Whether to rent or buy is the biggest money decision of most PCS moves, and the answer is mostly about how long you'll be here and how steady the local market is.
rent: Your tour is short (about two years or less) or your orders feel uncertain.
You want time to learn the area before committing to a neighborhood.
You'd rather not gamble on resale timing when you PCS out.
Your BAH comfortably covers rent in the areas you'd consider.
buy: You expect to be here three or more years.
You want to use your VA loan and build equity instead of paying rent.
You're comfortable with Colorado Springs prices, which were flat to slightly down over the past year (Zillow, September 2026).
You've found a neighborhood and commute you're confident about.
data.bottom_line: There is no universal right answer. Check the full tax bill, including any metro district, and price home insurance, which hail drives up along the Front Range. Run your BAH against the rent and home prices above, weigh your tour length, and talk to a lender and an agent who work with military families before you commit.

intro: The first month at a new duty station is mostly logistics. Knocking these out early makes everything else easier.

steps.title: Line up temporary lodging
steps.text: Book on-base lodging or a short-term rental before you arrive. You can claim Temporary Lodging Expense (TLE) for a limited number of days while you house-hunt.

steps.title: In-process and update DEERS
steps.text: Report to your unit and finance, and make sure DEERS and ID cards are current for every family member so TRICARE and base access work.

steps.title: Start with the Housing Office
steps.text: Check on-base availability and get the housing office's read on off-base neighborhoods before you sign anything.

steps.title: Register your vehicle and sort access
steps.text: Handle base access and the visitor-pass process for guests. If you register a vehicle in Colorado, nonresident service members can be exempt from the ownership tax (only) with form DR 2667, renewed every year; bring orders, military ID and a recent LES showing a non-Colorado withholding state.

steps.title: Enroll the kids in school
steps.text: On-post families attend Fountain-Fort Carson D8 schools; otherwise contact the gaining district early and bring records and immunizations. The School Liaison Office (719-526-6470) can help with the transfer.

steps.title: Set up healthcare
steps.text: Update your TRICARE enrollment so you can be seen at Evans Army Community Hospital or network providers.

data.a: The 4th Infantry Division, with three Stryker brigades and the 4th Combat Aviation Brigade, plus the 10th Special Forces Group (Airborne) and the 1st Space Brigade. It's known as the 'Mountain Post.'

Fountain (mainly Fountain-Fort Carson D8) and Security-Widefield (much of it Widefield D3) are closest; Cheyenne Mountain D12 and Academy D20 earned the state's top rating in 2025; the west side is closest to the mountains. On-post housing has about 3,200 homes.
No. The five on-post schools belong to Fountain-Fort Carson School District 8, and high schoolers living on post are bused to Fountain-Fort Carson High.

data.q: Anything to know about the altitude?
data.a: Yes. Colorado Springs sits at 6,035 feet, and new soldiers get 30 days to adjust before meeting Fort Carson fitness standards. Expect stronger sun, and snow anywhere from mid-October to late May.
Fort Carson is MHA CO046 (Colorado Springs). Use the calculator above for your grade.
